description: Hi! We're Team Rolinf 🚀 building "Earth Information Jukebox" for NASA Space Apps 2026.
summary:
NOFIRA is a decision-support prototype for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, built by Team Rolinf from Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. It is not a medical diagnostic system.
A single small error looks harmless, but a pattern of them can matter. NOFIRA does not simply count mistakes; it identifies how small operational deviations accumulate over time. It compares each astronaut with a personal baseline and calculates a transparent 0–100 Operational Deviation Index. When patterns build up, it generates explainable alerts that recommend human review.
Users can import NASA OSDR Inspiration4 data (OSD-569 and OSD-575), kept clearly separate from simulated demo data.
Limitations: NASA samples are sparse, the demo data is simulated, and the index is not clinically validated.
details:
NOFIRA is an astronaut health and operational performance monitoring prototype. A single small error looks harmless, but accumulating deviations can matter. NOFIRA compares each astronaut with a personal baseline and calculates a transparent 0–100 Operational Deviation Index from task time, errors, correction time and procedural deviations, with optional sleep and physiological indicators. When patterns build up (repeated errors, rising task or correction time, multi-indicator accumulation), it generates explainable alerts recommending human review. Every score can be inspected, missing values are never treated as zero, and identical inputs give identical results.
Benefits and impact: earlier visibility into gradual changes, structured performance monitoring, and a foundation for future integration with validated wearable and mission systems. It supports flight surgeons and mission control; it does not diagnose.
Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SVG charts, browser local storage, GitHub Pages. Includes a guided demo, simulation lab, NASA OSDR file import and explorer (OSD-569, OSD-575), CSV export and 12 engine tests.
Creativity: it treats small deviations as a pattern over time rather than isolated events, and keeps real NASA data, simulated data and derived analysis clearly separate.
Factors considered: NASA Inspiration4 samples are sparse timepoints, not continuous monitoring. Demo data is simulated, correlation is not causation, and the index is not clinically validated.
